Peel the pumpkin and cut into large slic: Arrange in a pot, sprinkle with sugar and leave for 4 hours.
Cook in its own juice over a low heat for 40 minutes.
Don’t add water; the pumpkin releases its own juice.
Halve the quinces and scoop out the seeds.
Arrange in a pot and add sugar, water and cloves.
Wrap the seeds in muslin and add them.
Cook over a low heat for 60 minutes until red.
The seeds give the red colour.
Add the semolina in a slow rain.
Cook for 8 minutes, stirring, until thick.
Pour into wet moulds and chill.
Wetting the moulds helps the pudding come out easily.
Add the dessert balls and cook over a low heat for 15 minutes.
Make the jelly according to the packet instructions.
Divide the fruit among the glasses.
When set, top with honeyed yogurt.
Kiwi and pineapple stop the jelly from setting.
Cook a custard with the milk, sugar, cornflour and flour.
Arrange the biscuits in the dish.
Pour over half the custard and lay the banana slices on it.
Add the bananas last so they don’t brown.
Layer the yogurt and halva in glasses.
Preheat the oven to 220 °C; melt the butter in a cast-iron pan.
Toss the apple slices with sugar and cinnamon in the pan for 3 minutes.
Whisk the eggs, flour and milk until smooth.
Pour the batter over the apples.
It deflates once out of the oven; serve immediately.
Melt the cheese in a pan.
Cook for 15 minutes until it releases its fat.
Add the sugar and let it melt.
Heat the milk, water and molasses and add them.
Stir until the liquid is absorbed.
Molasses takes the place of sugar.
Cut the bananas into thick slices.
Dip the slices in the chocolate.
Layer the custard and strawberries in bowls.
A strawberry sauce can also be made.
Dice the apples and put them in the ramekins.
Mix the oats, honey, butter and cinnamon.
Place on the artichokes and arrange in a pot.
Cook with oil, lemon, sugar, salt and 1 cup water for 25 minutes.
Make a filling with onion, rice and spices.
Arrange in a pot and add oil, lemon and 2 cups water.
